Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma
Bench: Subhash Chandra Sharma
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 80
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 11143 of 2022
Applicant :- Gaurav Alias Rohit Mishra And 2 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Lavkush Kumar Bhatt Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Vivek Kumar Singh Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Learned counsel for the applicants is permitted to delete the name of applicant no.1 from the array of parties during the course of the day, as the applicant no.1 has been sent to jail.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned counsel for the opposite party alongwith learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No.156 of 2017, under sections 498-A, 304-B I.P.C. & Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Mainpuri, District Mainpuri (Now it is in District Kannauj), during the pendency of trial.

It is submitted that on 28.10.2016 the deceased got burnt in the house while cooking in the kitchen by falling a lamp filled with kerosene oil, thereafter, she was taken to the hospital where during Gaurav Alias Rohit Mishra And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31764903/
1 treatment her dying declaration was recorded on 29.10.2016 by Nayab Tehsildar after taking certificate from the concerned doctor, thereafter, she died of burn injuries.
Further submitted that after lapse of two and a half months on 20.01.2017 an F.I.R. was lodged against the husband and the present applicants those are married nanad and nandoi u/s 498A,
304B I.P.C. & 3/4 D.P. Act.

entities.text: Gaurav Alias Rohit Mishra And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: During investigation the complicity of these applicants was not found to be established that was the reason they were exonerated but during trial while exercising its powers u/s 319 Cr.P.C. learned court concerned summoned these applicants for facing trial.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the applicants had no any interest in demand of dowry and harassment of the deceased but being relatives of the husband they have been named in the F.I.R. by concocting false story regarding demand of dowry and harassment after lapse of two and a half months from the alleged incident.
There is nothing on record against these applicants to show that they also made any demand of dowry and harassment of the deceased.

It is also submitted that the deceased was taken to the hospital where her dying declaration was recorded just after the next day of the alleged incident in which she clearly disclosed the cause of her death.

She stated that she was cooking in the kitchen meanwhile a lamp containing kerosene oil fell on her as a result she was set at fire and on her making hue and cry the members of the family and other villagers came there to rescue her.
She also stated that there was no fault of anyone.
This statement was recorded by the Nayab Tehsildar after taking certificate from the doctor providing treatment to the deceased when she was in conscious state.
Even during post-mortem no any other injury except burn was found on the person of the deceased.

It is further submitted that during investigation no any evidence was found against these applicants, therefore, their names were exonerated by the I.O.
but only on the basis of statement made by the informant and other witnesses related to the family of the informant these applicants have also been summoned by the learned court concerned for facing trial.
Therefore, the applicants are under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicants are released on bail, they would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail and urged that in this case these applicants were also making demand of dowry and harassment of the deceased with other family members of the husband.

When dying declaration was recorded the deceased cannot be said to remain in consciousness because she was in hundred percent burnt position and how concerned doctor gave certificate of consciousness, it cannot be said at this stage but this fact can only be cleared during cross-examination of the concerned doctor.
Therefore, the applicants are not entitled for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and perusal of record including dying declaration recorded by Nayab Tehslidar, the applicants are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
